title: VESPER Event Envelope
description: IC-001. An Event is an immutable statement that something HAPPENED. Events are never commands and never results. Authority: COC IC-001, ARCH-04, ARCH-25; REM-001; ADR-001.

event_id.description: Globally unique. The default idempotency key for consumers (INV-COORD-5).

schema_version.description: INV-SCHEMA-1: readers accept N and N-1; writers emit N. Never reused for different semantics.

type.description: Dotted typed event name, e.g. world.fact_updated, autonomy.trigger_fired, safety.stop_engaged.

source.description: Who observed or produced this. node_id is the cryptographic node identity from ADR-007, not a self-asserted name.

subject_kind.description: REM-004: the runtime is a first-class subject and is distinguishable from a human in every audit record.

subject.description: The entity this event is about. Ordering is total per (source, subject) and is NOT guaranteed across subjects (REM-001 s4.3).

observed_at_wall.description: DISPLAY AND POLICY WINDOWS ONLY. INV-COORD-4 forbids its use in ordering or supersession. CI-005 enforces this statically.

correlation_id.description: Links observation -> decision -> action -> verification. Survives purge (INV-OBS-2).

caused_by.description: Explicit causal reference to another event_id. The ONLY sanctioned way to express cross-subject happens-before, since cross-subject ordering is not guaranteed.

trigger_id.description: Mandatory on every autonomous action event and every recorded no-op (INV-TRIG-1, INV-TRIG-6).

sensitivity.description: Enforced by the telemetry writer at write time, never by caller discipline (INV-OBS-1). 'secret' payloads are never persisted.

trust_class.description: Taint. Propagates through summarisation, embedding and cache reuse (INV-AUTH-3). Absent or unrecognised is treated as retrieved_external.

provenance.description: Evidence references. A perception event with no provenance is malformed (ARCH-07).

payload_ref.description: Reference to a payload held in the separately-retained store. Content/reference separation is what lets purge remove data while the event skeleton and correlation chain survive (INV-PRIV-5, INV-SCHEMA-2).

payload.description: Typed per event type. MUST be empty when sensitivity is 'sensitive' or 'secret' -- use payload_ref instead.

hlc.description: Hybrid logical clock. Ordering is lexicographic on (physical_ms, logical, node_id); node_id is the tie-breaker so the order is TOTAL, not partial. This is the ONLY ordering input (INV-COORD-4).

allOf.$comment: Sensitive payloads must not be inline. Enforced structurally rather than by convention.
